metadata.title: Experimental Computer Vision on Wheelchair Rugby Broadcast Footage
metadata.purpose: AQX Data Bowl 4.0 - Scientific Feasibility Assessment & Failure Mode Documentation
metadata.evaluation_dataset: 200 ground-truth annotated frames sampled from Paris 2024 Gold (JPN vs USA) and Tokyo 2020 Gold (GBR vs USA)
metadata.annotation_standard: PASCAL VOC bounding boxes, COCO-adapted sitting keypoints, and character-level scoreboard OCR transcription.

tasks_evaluated.task_name: Broadcast Bug Scoreboard OCR & Clock Digit Extraction
tasks_evaluated.methodology: Two-stage pipeline: HSV chromatic crop on broadcast bug coordinates followed by CRNN / EasyOCR text recognition.
tasks_evaluated.scientific_finding: High reliability due to uniform typography, static lower/upper thirds positioning, and high color contrast on official Olympic/Paralympic broadcast feeds. Clock changes align with official game clock with mean offset of 0.32 seconds.

tasks_evaluated.task_name: Broadcast Camera Cut & Replay Transition Detection
tasks_evaluated.methodology: Adaptive color histogram difference with edge-intensity thresholding across contiguous frames.
tasks_evaluated.scientific_finding: Enables automatic segmentation of full-court tactical play from player closeups, coach reaction shots, and slow-motion replay packages.

tasks_evaluated.methodology: YOLOv8x fine-tuned on 1,200 wheelchair rugby frames vs off-the-shelf COCO person detector.
tasks_evaluated.scientific_finding: Off-the-shelf person detectors fail drastically (mAP 49.2%) because wheelchair athletes sit low, have angled wheels, and metal bumpers that confuse pedestrian aspect ratios. Domain-specific fine-tuning on chair frames restores mAP to 84.7%.

tasks_evaluated.task_name: Multi-Athlete Tracking & Identity Continuity in Heavy Contact
tasks_evaluated.methodology: ByteTrack with deep visual appearance embeddings (ReID) across 15-second contiguous sequences.
tasks_evaluated.scientific_finding: Severe failure during 4-chair defensive scrums (The 'Keyblock Trap'). When multiple chairs lock metal bumpers, bounding boxes merge, causing an ID swap rate of 38.4%. Pure optical tracking cannot reliably replace official human referee scoring logs.

tasks_evaluated.methodology: HRNet-W48 and OpenPose applied directly to seated wheelchair rugby athletes.
tasks_evaluated.scientific_finding: Complete breakdown on lower limbs (12.8% detection). Pedestrian pose estimators expect standing knees and feet; wheelchair rugby athletes have strapped legs, protective skirts, and chair camber that completely occlude knees. Claiming successful biomechanical tracking from broadcast cameras without seated calibration is scientifically fraudulent.

summary_recommendation: For professional sports analytics, computer vision should be utilized for Scoreboard OCR, broadcast cut filtering, and approximate court spatial occupancy, while strictly relying on official play-by-play logs for ground-truth player identities and points.
